articles.title: County Championship cricket: Craig Overton, Jack Leach help Somerset remain top with crushing win at Leicestershire
articles.summary: After title rivals Warwickshire claimed victory inside two days against Glamorgan, leaders Somerset responded with aplomb against Leicestershire to clinch 377-run victory and return top of the Rothesay County Championship as Craig Overton and Jack Leach stood out
articles.body:
After title rivals Warwickshire claimed victory inside two days against Glamorgan, leaders Somerset responded with aplomb.

Henry Nicholls' unbeaten 100 helped the visitors declare on 316-5 to set Leicestershire an insurmountable victory target of 523.

The real question was whether Somerset could wrap up this latest triumph with a day to spare and Leicestershire only managed to bat out 45.1 overs, with Overton the pick of the bowlers - 4-33 - and England's forgotten man Leach taking 3-30 to dismiss the hosts for 145.

Nottinghamshire , who are also in the title picture, responded to being dismissed for 104 at Trent Bridge on day three to fight back and take control against Hampshire .

During a 19-wicket day, Hampshire were dismissed for 304 before England's teenage prospect Manny Lumsden ripped through Nottinghamshire's top order in sensational fashion.

After Haseeb Hameed had watched Nottinghamshire collapse to set only 178 for victory, Olly Stone and Dillon Pennington ran amok to reduce Hampshire to 61-6 at stumps and set up a tantalising final day, with England U19 international Ben Mayes on 21 not out.

Essex 's relegation fears increased after they suffered defeat by an innings and 106 runs at Yorkshire .

After Essex were all out for 171 - despite an unbeaten fifty by debutant George Bell - they followed on and were rolled for 113, with home bowler Kuldeep Yadav able to claim match figures of 10-120.

Ben Foakes made 54 to help Surrey to 294-7 against Sussex before bad light in Hove ensured they will trail by 99 runs ahead of Friday's final day.

In Division Two, Northamptonshire piled the pressure on promotion rivals Kent after they won by six wickets at Worcestershire , who were all out for 182 in their second innings, and George Bartlett's unbeaten 19 got his team over the line in pursuit of 94 at New Road.

Kent have dropped to third but will return to second if they can bat out day four at Derbyshire or chase down an unlikely total of 434. After the hosts declared on 352-8, visiting openers Zak Crawley and Ben Compton survived nine balls before the close.

Leaders Durham are in control after Middlesex were reduced to 55-2 in pursuit of 424.

Rocky Flintoff made a first-class best 57 not out, but Lancashire are 120-6 with 128 runs required for victory over Gloucestershire .

articles.title: England vs Pakistan: Brook, Smith, Lawrence and Robinson push hosts towards third Test win
articles.summary: England's charge towards a two-day victory in the final Test against Pakistan is only halted by rain at Edgbaston.
articles.body:
Third Rothesay Test, Edgbaston (day two of five)

Pakistan 133 (Shakeel 43; Tongue 4-42) & 52-2 (Robinson 2-10)

England 453 (Brook 75, Smith 69, Lawrence 65, Gay 60, Robinson 50; Razaullah 4-148)

England's charge towards a two-day win in the final Test against Pakistan was only halted by rain at Edgbaston.

The tourists were battling for survival on 52-2 - 268 adrift of making England bat again - when the bad weather intervened for a second and final occasion in Birmingham.

The time was 17:07 BST. With the possibility of an extra half an hour available to force a result, play could have continued until 19:00 if conditions had allowed.

Given the fragility of the Pakistan batting - the tourists have not reached 200 or batted for more than 51 overs in the series - there was a real possibility England would earn victory inside two days after Ollie Robinson reduced the visitors to 0-2.

Instead, the players will return on Friday, when England will complete a 3-0 series clean sweep.

The eventual outcome of this match was barely in doubt when England began Thursday on 156-4, leading by 23.

Contributions of 75 from Harry Brook, 69 by Jamie Smith, 65 scored by Dan Lawrence and 50 from Robinson pushed England to 453, a huge first-innings lead of 320.

The only disappointment was that no England batter pushed on to make a century, meaning Ben Duckett's ton against New Zealand at Trent Bridge will remain the home side's only hundred of the summer.

Dominant England set target for Pakistan at Edgbaston

One of the criticisms of the previous England regime, under captain Ben Stokes and coach Brendon McCullum, was their inability to finish series strongly.

England have lost the final Test in each of their past six series. Some of their worst performances in the Bazball era came in dead rubbers after a series had been won, notably at home to Sri Lanka in 2024 and away to New Zealand later the same year.

Stokes often said he did not like the word "ruthless" and there were plenty of times his side lacked ruthlessness. On this occasion, Root's England are showing their ruthless side.

The quality of the opposition should be taken into account - Stokes' England would have comfortably beaten this poor Pakistan side. The hosts also had the better of the conditions on Thursday, batting under blue sky then bowling when it got dark overhead.

But, under Root, England are showing a new-found calmness, along with a willingness to find the right tempo to their batting. The way they extended their lead on the second day was an example of a more mature approach.

And, in Robinson, they have a bowler in the form of his life, a purple patch England will hope carries through the winter and to next summer's Ashes.

Batters impress but miss out on hundreds

Given England's dominance over Pakistan, it is curious that none of their batters have registered a century in the series and now will not get another chance.

Duckett's sole ton means England will end a six-Test home summer with their fewest number of individual hundreds.

Brook, Lawrence and Smith all impressed, and all will be disappointed they missed out on three figures.

A stand of 86 between Brook and Lawrence was full of intent at the beginning of the day, with Lawrence the aggressor. Busy running was a feature of the stand, until Brook attempted a needless single to mid-wicket and was run out at the non-striker's end.

Lawrence has made three half-centuries since being recalled at the beginning of this series, probably enough to earn a place in South Africa in December. This is his 17th Test and he gave an audible cry of frustration when he chopped on off Mohammad Imran, extending a wait for a maiden hundred.

Smith suffered a tough Ashes tour, yet has shown signs of rehabilitation with bat and wicketkeeping gloves this summer. On a ground where he has had plenty of previous success, he muscled the ball through the leg side before he offered a tame return catch to Razaullah.

Robinson can do no wrong at the moment. He swiped through the leg side, including a massive six into the Hollies Stand, for his second half-century in Test cricket. Robinson's previous 50 came against India in Ranchi in 2024, his last before being dropped. Now he is indispensable.

Even Jofra Archer got involved, heaving two sixes of his own. He was left unbeaten on 32 when last man Josh Tongue was caught behind.

England denied chance to build on Robinson strikes

Pakistan's innings began after tea, leaving England one session to produce the first two-day finish in a Test in this country since 2000.

With Jordan Cox keeping in place of Smith, who has a bruised finger, Robinson made the sort of start that made a two-day finish a real possibility.

From the first ball of the innings, Saim Ayub needlessly edged to Brook at second slip. In the same over, Abdullah Shafique's crooked bat resulted in an edge to Root at first slip.

To their credit, Azan Awais and Shan Masood survived 12 overs in the gloom, even if Masood survived a tough chance to third slip Duckett off the bowling of Gus Atkinson.

articles.title: England vs Pakistan: Ollie Robinson strikes twice in first over of second innings as hosts dominate day two of third Test at Edgbaston
articles.summary: Ollie Robinson dismissed Saim Ayub for a pair and Abdullah Shafique in first over of Pakistan second innings; England seamer has 28 wickets in four Tests this summer, at an average of 7.75 apiece; watch day three live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10.15am, Friday
articles.body:
Pakistan's score at stumps actually represented somewhat of a recovery after their prospects looked even gloomier than the darkening skies overhead when reduced to 0-2 in Ollie Robinson's first over.

Robinson (2-10) saw off Saim Ayub first ball - the opener, one of four players flown straight into the team after seven were axed from the touring squad, out for a pair - before Abdullah Shafique also nicked to the slips three deliveries later.

It means that Robinson now has 28 wickets across his four Test appearances this summer, taking them at a staggering 7.75 apiece. In this series that improves even further to 6.66.

Joe Root's grab at slip to send back Shafique moved him one clear of Australia's Steve Smith and onto 220 in their personal battle to claim the most catches by an outfielder in Test cricket.

The clatter of wickets didn't follow as it had in Pakistan's first innings, with Azan Awais (29no) and Shan Masood (21no) sharing a fifty stand before the rain arrived - albeit Masood was put down on 13 by Ben Duckett, his third spill of the Test, off the unfortunate Gus Atkinson.

Brook, Lawrence and Smith all miss out with Test tons looming

Earlier, England were bowled out for 452, earning a 320-run lead on first innings as Dan Lawrence (65), Jamie Smith (69) and Robinson (50) added half-centuries to those notched by Emilio Gay (60) and Harry Brook (75) on day one.

Brook added 23 to his overnight total before he was the first wicket to fall on the second morning, just at the point where he and Dan Lawrence - who had stormed through to a 47-ball fifty - had seemingly broken Pakistan's spirits with 73 scored off the opening 10 overs of the day.

The breakthrough was a gift, Brook practically running himself out as he called for a risky single to midwicket, where Masood did the honours with a direct hit.

The scoring didn't slow as Smith joined Lawrence at the crease, the pair putting on 64 together before Lawrence was left kicking himself as he chopped one from Mohammad Imran (2-47) back onto his stumps just before lunch.

Smith was the next through to fifty - off 54 balls - but failed to convert as, after Gus Atkinson (19) was bowled by a beauty from Imran, Smith chipped one back to the fired-up Razaullah (4-148).

While he was okay to bat, Smith would later be absent from the field - Jordan Cox subbing in at wicketkeeper - with the regular gloveman nursing an injured finger from the first day.

Robinson, hitting a second Test half-century, and Jofra Archer (32no) had some fun lower down the order, finding the boundary - or clearing it - with regularity as England pushed their total above 400 and lead beyond 300 before the innings was finally ended.

Pakistan carried their increasingly timid approach in the field over into the start of their second innings, and a two-day finish briefly looked a possibility after Robinson's double strike in the first over, before Azan and Masood showed some much-needed resilience and the rain intervened.

"Saim Ayub, in particular, struggled. The truth is he shouldn't be here. He came from the CPL [Caribbean Premier League] and hasn't played first-class cricket in 11 months.

"I don't know who thinks it's the right thing to fly someone over from foreign conditions, and think they'll be fine in these conditions against a Duke's ball and Ollie Robinson's bowling attack? It's showing disrespect to Test match cricket.

"The players who are here, their friends and room-mates have been axed. People who have got five-fors have been axed.

"How you treat players is so important. It's a two-way thing when players are presented with a Test cap. You're expected to meet the core values of representing Pakistan, but the team needs to look after the players in return.

"That goes the moment you send seven people home. People start looking after themselves. Why should I bother about a team that doesn't bother about me and has sent my team-mates home between Tests?

"This Pakistan side, not only are they in poor form, they look like a team that says, 'what will be, will be', and just looks after itself."

articles.title: JP Atray Tournament ends 34-year innings as packed cricket calendar forces closure
articles.summary: After 34 years of cricketing history, the All India JP Atray Cricket Tournament has come to a close. Esteemed as a pre-season event held 30 times in honor of...
articles.body:
The All India JP Atray Cricket Tournament, a prominent pre-season fixture that has been part of the Indian cricket landscape since 1992, has brought the curtain down on its 34-year innings. The tournament, which was held 30 times over the past 34 years as a tribute to former Haryana ADGP Jai Prakash Atray, will no longer be staged from this year. The tournament committee and the Atray family have decided to close the chapter, bringing an end to one of India's long-running domestic one-day tournaments.

The JP Atray Tournament was played in the 50-over format and traditionally served as a pre-season curtain-raiser for Indian cricket. It was affiliated with the Punjab Cricket Association (PCA) and received annual approval from the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI). Over the decades, the tournament featured a long list of Indian stars, including Kapil Dev, Yashpal Sharma, Sourav Ganguly, MS Dhoni, Virender Sehwag, Yuvraj Singh, Harbhajan Singh, Ravindra Jadeja, Jasprit Bumrah, Rohit Sharma, Cheteshwar Pujara, Ajinkya Rahane, Irfan Pathan, Gautam Gambhir, Shikhar Dhawan, Shubman Gill, Rishabh Pant, Hardik Pandya and Chetan Sharma. According to the release, as many as 140 cricketers who participated in the tournament subsequently went on to represent India. Several also returned to play in the JP Atray Tournament after having already represented the country across formats.

The primary reason for the tournament's closure is the increasingly packed cricket calendar. With international and domestic commitments filling the schedule, top players are no longer readily available for competitions such as the JP Atray Tournament. The rapid growth of T20 cricket and the emergence of numerous state-level T20 leagues have further squeezed the calendar, while the availability of grounds has also become a major challenge. While the men's tournament has ended, the Rama Atray Tournament for women cricketers will continue. Its seventh edition is scheduled to commence later this month in Chandigarh. The Atray family expressed gratitude to the cricket associations, particularly the BCCI and PCA, organisers led by founder organising secretary Capt Sushil Kapoor, as well as players, sponsors, coaches, umpires, scorers, managers, ground staff and well-wishers who contributed to the tournament's success. "A huge sense of gratitude to all our well wishers and friends ...," said Vivek Atray.

articles.body: England strengthened their grip on the third Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston on Thursday, piling up 453 in their first innings before reducing the visitors to 52/2 at stumps on Day 2.Having started the day with a 23-run lead, England added another 297 runs across the first two sessions to take a massive 320-run first-innings lead. Pakistan then endured a nightmare start to their second innings, losing both openers in Ollie Robinson’s opening over.Shan Masood and Azan Awais offered some resistance before rain and bad light brought an early end to play. Pakistan still trail by 268 runs, with eight wickets in hand.England’s batters pile on the runsResuming on 156/4, England’s middle and lower order kept Pakistan’s bowlers under pressure throughout the morning and afternoon sessions. Harry Brook top-scored with 75, while Jamie Smith made 69 and Dan Lawrence contributed 65. Emilio Gay also struck a fluent 60 before Ollie Robinson added a rapid 50 off 47 balls.Five England batters passed fifty, but none could convert their starts into a century. The hosts were eventually bowled out for 453 shortly before tea.Pakistan debutant Razaullah was their most successful bowler, finishing with 4/148. He had moments of promise but struggled to contain England’s scoring rate, while Mohammad Ali and Mohammad Imran picked up two wickets each.Robinson rocks Pakistan with double strikePakistan needed a strong response after being asked to bat again with a 320-run deficit, but Robinson immediately exposed their top order. articles.body: India produced another dominant performance with bat and ball to beat Bangladesh by 40 runs and storm into the final of the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Thursday. After posting 149/6 in their 20 overs, India’s bowlers delivered under pressure to restrict Bangladesh to 109/7, successfully defending what initially appeared to be a modest total on a slow pitch.The victory extended India’s unbeaten run in the tournament and secured their place in a 10th successive Women’s Asia Cup final. They will face the winner of the second semi-final between defending champions Sri Lanka and Pakistan in the title clash on September 13.Shafali’s blazing 64 lifts IndiaBangladesh won the toss and opted to field, but Shafali Varma made the most of the opportunity to put India on the front foot.The explosive opener smashed 64 off 40 balls, hitting seven fours and three sixes, as she held India’s innings together after vice-captain Smriti Mandhana fell for just two. Shafali rode her luck after being dropped three times but made Bangladesh pay with an attacking knock that gave India a competitive total.Captain Harmanpreet Kaur struggled for fluency but contributed 24 off 28 balls, including two sixes, while Richa Ghosh added an important 21 off 16 deliveries. Deepti Sharma then provided the late impetus with a quick 13 off six balls, helping India finish just short of 150.Deepti spins Bangladesh into troubleBangladesh needed 150 to reach the final but struggled to maintain momentum throughout their chase. Deepti Sharma once again proved the difference with the ball, claiming 3/26 in four overs and repeatedly breaking Bangladesh's resistance.Nandani Sharma also impressed, taking 2/10 from two overs, including the final wicket of the innings. Bangladesh’s top order showed glimpses of resistance, with Dilara Akter scoring 21 off 26 balls and Shorna Akter hitting a brisk 22 off 18. But the batting line-up failed to absorb India's sustained pressure.The Tigresses lost wickets at regular intervals as India tightened their grip on the chase. With the required rate climbing, Bangladesh could only reach 109/7 in 20 overs, falling 40 runs short.The innings ended in fitting fashion for India, with Nandani Sharma dismissing Rabeya Khan hit-wicket. Khan attempted to slog a slower delivery but ended up dislodging the stumps with her bat while completing the shot.India eye another Asia Cup titleIndia’s latest victory keeps their unbeaten campaign intact and sends them into yet another Asia Cup final. articles.title: Joe Root's struggles and England century drought against Pakistan the only concerns from improved post-Bazball batting, says Nasser Hussain
articles.summary: England in complete control of third Test against Pakistan with tourists 268 runs behind at stumps; England dominate day two with the bat but Nasser Hussain highlights two areas for improvement; watch day three live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10.15am on Friday
articles.body:
England piled on 453 runs to establish a commanding first-innings lead of 320 in the third Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston.

The hosts were firmly in control and on course for a 3-0 series sweep, with Pakistan closing on 52-2, still 268 runs adrift, when rain curtailed play.

"I've liked the tempo of the batting in this series," former England captain Hussain said.

"We talked about it earlier in the Bazball era, England going too hard and not seizing opportunities.

"They've got the tempo right, especially through the middle order with Harry Brook, Jamie Smith, Dan Lawrence and Gus Atkinson.

"I know it's a poor Pakistan bowling attack, but even Josh Tongue and Jofra Archer have contributed with the bat.

"I like Emilio Gay's tempo at the top of the order. He bats time and knows when to absorb pressure. English cricket, and this side in particular, have been crying out for that."

Despite the overwhelming positives, Hussain highlighted two areas England have yet to address during the Pakistan series.

Root's four dismissals have all been lbw, with the world's second-highest Test run-scorer continuing to wrestle with that mode of dismissal.

"Obviously, there are two boxes they haven't ticked," Hussain explained.

"Their greatest player is struggling with one specific type of dismissal: lbw.

"It's so obvious he's struggling. He tried to address it in the first innings, made a technical adjustment and then got out lbw again."

'England need to convert starts to big scores'

Meanwhile, England's wait for a hundred has reached historic levels.

Brook (75), Smith (69), Lawrence (65), Gay (60) and Ollie Robinson (50) have all reached fifty without kicking on to three figures.

A total of 14 half-centuries have been scored across the series without a single hundred, the first time that has happened in a Test series in England since the 1888 Ashes.

"The other one is getting hundreds," Hussain added.

"You can beat Pakistan with 40s, 50s and 60s. To beat Australia, or the New Zealand side we saw earlier in the summer, you need big hundreds and massive scores

"England just need to convert those starts into big scores."

Reflecting on the absence of a century in the Test series, former England bowler Stuart Broad has called for a reassessment of what constitutes a good score after a scorching summer has made conditions favourable for bowlers.

Broad argued that some scores this summer have been every bit as valuable as centuries on flatter pitches.

"Top-order batting has been very difficult in this series," Broad said.

"Root, England's best-ever player, has struggled for runs in this series. If he's struggling, it's OK for everyone else to struggle.

"We can't praise the likes of Ollie Robinson, who is getting 20-odd wickets at an average of around 6.00, and also say, 'We should be getting more centuries.'

"To be honest, this summer I think a 60 has felt like a hundred.

"You've had to work as hard for a 60 on these pitches as you would for a hundred on a normal Test match surface."
